knowledge:
- key_parameters: formula=A formula of the form `pvalue ~ covariate` specifying the p-value and covariate columns ;; data=A data frame containing the variables in the formula ;; alpha=The nominal significance level for FDR or FWER control (e.g., 0.1) ;; adjustment_type=Character string specifying the multiple testing procedure, such as "bonferroni" for FWER control (default is FDR control) ;; m_groups=A table or vector specifying the total number of hypotheses in each covariate bin, required when working with incomplete/truncated p-value lists
- alternatives: p.adjust(..., method="BH")=The standard Benjamini-Hochberg procedure, which does not use covariate information and has lower power ;; p.adjust(..., method="bonferroni")=The standard Bonferroni correction for FWER control, which is less powerful than weighted Bonferroni
- when_to_use: Use when performing high-dimensional hypothesis testing (e.g., RNA-Seq differential expression, eQTL, GWAS, proteomics) where an auxiliary covariate is available that is informative of test power or prior probability, independent of p-values under the null, and not driving the correlation structure of the tests.
- pitfalls: Using a covariate that is dependent on the p-values under the null (e.g., using estimated log fold change instead of baseMean in RNA-Seq) which invalidates FDR control ;; Using a covariate that drives the correlation structure among tests (e.g., genomic coordinates in GWAS due to linkage disequilibrium) ;; Failing to check stratified p-value histograms to ensure they are well-calibrated (uniform distribution for large p-values across all strata).

workflows.name: standard_ihw_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform independent hypothesis weighting for FDR or FWER control using a complete list of p-values and a continuous covariate.
input: deRes.csv (a data frame containing p-values and a continuous covariate such as baseMean from differential expression analysis)
workflows.stages: 1. Run the IHW procedure using the formula interface ;; 2. Retrieve the total number of rejections ;; 3. Extract adjusted p-values and weights ;; 4. Generate diagnostic plots of weights and decision boundaries ;; 5. Convert the results to a data frame for downstream analysis ;; 6. Optionally perform FWER control using the Bonferroni adjustment type.
workflows.code:
ihwRes <- ihw(pvalue ~ baseMean,  data = deRes, alpha = 0.1)
rejections(ihwRes)
head(adj_pvalues(ihwRes))
sum(adj_pvalues(ihwRes) <= 0.1, na.rm = TRUE) == rejections(ihwRes)
head(weights(ihwRes))
c(nbins(ihwRes), nfolds(ihwRes))
weights(ihwRes, levels_only = TRUE)
plot(ihwRes)
plot(ihwRes, what = "decisionboundary")
ihwResDf <- as.data.frame(ihwRes)
ihwBonferroni <- ihw(pvalue ~ baseMean, data = deRes, alpha = 0.1, adjustment_type = "bonferroni")

workflows.name: incomplete_pvalues_ihw
workflows.intent: Perform independent hypothesis weighting when only a subset of low p-values is reported or available.
input: sim.csv (the full dataset containing the covariate to calculate group sizes)
simSub.csv (the filtered dataset containing only the reported low p-values)
workflows.stages: 1. Discretize the continuous covariate into bins using groups_by_filter ;; 2. Calculate the total number of hypotheses per bin using table ;; 3. Run IHW on the filtered dataset by specifying the group factor and passing the table of group sizes to m_groups.
workflows.code:
nbins <- 20
sim <- mutate(sim, group = groups_by_filter(X, nbins))
m_groups  <- table(sim$group)
ihwS <- ihw(p ~ group, alpha = 0.1, data = filter(sim, reported), m_groups = m_groups)
ihwS
